Before you act on this

  • Night, stability class F on this brief: very stable air is among the conditions that make a dispersion estimate unreliable: "Gas concentrations within the cloud can remain high far from the source." T43
  • A modelled layer is drawn: it is one scenario; the ERG: "These adjustments should only be made by technically qualified personnel." erg2024-en-pdf p. 282
  • SLAB, whose time-bounded area is every level's extent check here, on a pressurised jet: 1991 EPA evaluation: within a factor of 2 on 0/6 Desert Tortoise (ammonia), 0/7 Goldfish (hydrofluoric acid); under-predicts pressurised jets by 2.5 to 3. epa-dense-gas-evaluation-1991 p. 94
  • People indoors: the modelled layers are outdoor concentrations; this brief estimates no indoor concentration T42

Guide 124, Gases - Toxic and/or Corrosive - Oxidizing: public safety

  • CALL 911. Then call emergency response telephone number on shipping paper. If shipping paper not available or no answer, refer to appropriate telephone number listed on the inside back cover. p. 180
  • Keep unauthorized personnel away. p. 180
  • Stay upwind, uphill and/or upstream. p. 180
  • Many gases are heavier than air and will spread along the ground and collect in low or confined areas (sewers, basements, tanks, etc.). p. 180
  • Ventilate closed spaces before entering, but only if properly trained and equipped. p. 180
  • PROTECTIVE CLOTHING
  • Wear positive pressure self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA). p. 180
  • Wear chemical protective clothing that is specifically recommended by the manufacturer when there is NO RISK OF FIRE. p. 180
  • Structural firefighters' protective clothing provides thermal protection but only limited chemical protection. p. 180
  • EVACUATION
  • Immediate precautionary measure
  • Isolate spill or leak area for at least 100 meters (330 feet) in all directions. p. 180
  • Spill
  • See Table 1 - Initial Isolation and Protective Action Distances. p. 180

Response guidance

● Retrieved 10/25/2026 17:35

ERG 2024 Guide 124: Gases - Toxic and/or Corrosive - Oxidizing

Potential hazards

HEALTH

  • TOXIC and/or CORROSIVE; may be fatal if inhaled or absorbed through skin. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Fire will produce irritating, corrosive and/or toxic gases. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Contact with gas or liquefied gas may cause burns, severe injury and/or frostbite. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Runoff from fire control or dilution water may cause environmental contamination. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]

FIRE OR EXPLOSION

  • Substance does not burn but will support combustion. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Vapors from liquefied gas are initially heavier than air and spread along ground. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • These are strong oxidizers and will react vigorously or explosively with many materials including fuels. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • May ignite combustibles (wood, paper, oil, clothing, etc.). [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Some will react violently with air, moist air and/or water. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Cylinders exposed to fire may vent and release toxic and/or corrosive gas through pressure relief devices. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Containers may explode when heated. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Ruptured cylinders may rocket. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]

Public safety

  • CALL 911. Then call emergency response telephone number on shipping paper. If shipping paper not available or no answer, refer to appropriate telephone number listed on the inside back cover. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Keep unauthorized personnel away. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Stay upwind, uphill and/or upstream. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Many gases are heavier than air and will spread along the ground and collect in low or confined areas (sewers, basements, tanks, etc.). [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Ventilate closed spaces before entering, but only if properly trained and equipped. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]

PROTECTIVE CLOTHING

  • Wear positive pressure self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA). [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Wear chemical protective clothing that is specifically recommended by the manufacturer when there is NO RISK OF FIRE. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]
  • Structural firefighters' protective clothing provides thermal protection but only limited chemical protection. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]

EVACUATION

Immediate precautionary measure

  • Isolate spill or leak area for at least 100 meters (330 feet) in all directions. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]

Spill

  • See Table 1 - Initial Isolation and Protective Action Distances. [erg2024-en-pdf#p180]

Emergency response

FIRE

  • CAUTION: These materials do not burn but will support combustion. Some will react violently with water. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]

Small Fire

  • Contain fire and let burn. If fire must be fought, water spray or fog is recommended. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • Water only; no dry chemical, CO2 or Halon®. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • Do not get water inside containers. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • If it can be done safely, move undamaged containers away from the area around the fire. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • Damaged cylinders should be handled only by specialists. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]

Fire Involving Tanks

  • Fight fire from maximum distance or use unmanned master stream devices or monitor nozzles. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • Cool containers with flooding quantities of water until well after fire is out. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • Do not direct water at source of leak or safety devices; icing may occur. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • Withdraw immediately in case of rising sound from venting safety devices or discoloration of tank. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • ALWAYS stay away from tanks in direct contact with flames. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • For massive fire, use unmanned master stream devices or monitor nozzles; if this is impossible, withdraw from area and let fire burn. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]

SPILL OR LEAK

  • Do not touch or walk through spilled material. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • Keep combustibles (wood, paper, oil, etc.) away from spilled material. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • Stop leak if you can do it without risk. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • Use water spray to reduce vapors or divert vapor cloud drift. Avoid allowing water runoff to contact spilled material. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • Do not direct water at spill or source of leak. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • If possible, turn leaking containers so that gas escapes rather than liquid. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • Prevent entry into waterways, sewers, basements or confined areas. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • Isolate area until gas has dispersed. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]
  • Ventilate the area. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]

FIRST AID

Refer to the “General First Aid” section.

Specific First Aid:

  • Clothing frozen to the skin should be thawed before being removed. [erg2024-en-pdf#p181]

Annex A: Data limits and sources

Limits

  • verify_in_erg_app opens PHMSA's ERG app at this material, spill size, period, surface, wind and point. Compare its drawing with this footprint. Its link specification is the ERG 2020 app's. The app may draw ERG 2020 distances; this footprint uses ERG 2024.
  • The structures dataset holds selected facilities, so a school, hospital, fire station or police station it omits is not listed [USGS National Structures Dataset service description].
  • Nursing homes are those certified by Medicare or Medicaid; assisted living facilities are not listed [CMS Nursing Home Provider Information].
  • People in nursing facilities, correctional facilities, college housing and other group quarters are counted by population_at_risk, not here.
  • A waterway counts once per named stream or 3DHP mainstem, and its reaches inside are summed [USGS 3D Hydrography Program].
  • Drinking water intakes are not published, so waterways are listed, not intakes [Safe Drinking Water Act section 1433].
  • Rail lines count by segment between network nodes, so one line can count more than once [NTAD North American Rail Network Lines].
  • Grade crossings are the at-grade crossings of the FRA inventory, public and private; bridges and underpasses are not counted [NTAD Railroad Grade Crossings].
  • A facility just outside the footprint is not listed unless buffer_m is set.
  • Distances are straight lines from the footprint's upwind edge, not drive times.
  • Trauma level, burn care and toxicology capability are not in these datasets; confirm capability with each hospital.
  • Hospitals listed are those registered with Medicare that report emergency services [CMS Hospital General Information].
  • Emergency services means the hospital reports providing them, not that it has capacity now [CMS Hospital General Information].
  • Bed counts are the Provider of Services bed counts, not beds available now [CMS Provider of Services].
  • A hospital is flagged when the straight line to it from the upwind edge crosses the protective action zone.
  • Roads are not read, so a flagged hospital may have a route around the zone.
  • 252 hospitals could not be placed by address and are not ranked, of 4,495 hospitals with emergency services [CMS Hospital General Information, as of 07/22/2026].
  • unplaced_in_states names the unplaced hospitals in each state listed.
  • Each line is printed as the ERG prints it, with its PDF page, as a quotation.
  • The incident selects the lines; selection.omitted names every line left out and why.
  • The guide refers to the General First Aid section, which is not reprinted here.
  • TIGERweb returned no basemap image, so the sketch draws no roads.
